questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define density and state its unit. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Describe an experiment to determine the density of a piece of stone (irregularly shaped object). Include in your description: a list of apparatus needed, a diagram of the set-up, the procedure you will use to collect data, how the data is used to obtain the density of the stone, and any precaution taken to minimize error. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Density is the **mass per unit volume** of a substance, $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V}$. Unit: $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$ (or $\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$).

(ii) **Apparatus:** electronic balance, measuring cylinder, water, thread.

**Set-up:** a measuring cylinder holding water, the stone hanging from a thread, to be lowered in.

**Procedure:** 1. Measure the mass $m$ of the stone on the balance. 2. Pour water in the cylinder and read the volume $V_1$. 3. Tie the stone to the thread, lower it fully into the water without splashing and read the new volume $V_2$.

**Calculation:** volume of the stone $V = V_2 - V_1$; density $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V_2 - V_1}$.

**Precautions:** read the meniscus at eye level; make sure no air bubbles cling to the stone; use enough water to cover it completely; repeat and average.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define pressure. *[1 mark]*

A rectangular block $0.01\,\mathrm{m}$ by $0.02\,\mathrm{m}$ by $0.04\,\mathrm{m}$ has a mass of $0.064\,\mathrm{kg}$. Calculate:

(ii) the area of the largest face of the block; (iii) the weight of the block; (iv) the pressure the block will exert on a surface when lying on its largest face. *[2 + 2 + 2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Pressure is the **force acting normally per unit area**: $P = \dfrac{F}{A}$.

(ii) Largest face: $0.02\times 0.04 = 8\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m^2}$.

(iii) Weight $= mg = 0.064\times 10 = 0.64\,\mathrm{N}$.

(iv) $P = \dfrac{0.64}{8\times10^{-4}} = 800\,\mathrm{Pa}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define elastic limit. *[2 marks]*

(ii) A copper wire is stretched by a force which is gradually increased in magnitude until the wire breaks. Sketch a force-extension graph for the wire. On your graph indicate the elastic limit. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The elastic limit is the **maximum force (or extension) up to which a material returns to its original length when the force is removed**.

(ii) The graph is a straight line through the origin (extension proportional to force) up to the elastic limit, then it curves towards the extension axis until the wire breaks. Mark the elastic limit where the line stops being straight. *(Figure to be produced.)*

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define a longitudinal wave and give an example. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Describe an experiment to determine the speed of sound in air. Include: a list of apparatus needed, a diagram of the set-up, the procedure you will use to collect data, how the data is used to obtain the speed of sound, and any precaution taken to minimize error. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A longitudinal wave is one in which the particles of the medium **vibrate parallel to the direction in which the wave travels**. Example: sound.

(ii) **Echo method.** Apparatus: a tape measure or trundle wheel, a stopwatch, a large flat wall, a hand clapper or a starting gun.

**Procedure:** stand a measured distance $d$ from the wall; clap and start the stopwatch, stop it when the echo returns; repeat several times and take the mean time $t$.

**Calculation:** the sound travels $2d$ in time $t$, so $v = \dfrac{2d}{t}$.

**Precautions:** stand far enough (at least 50 m) so the echo is distinct; repeat and average; time from the clap, not from the movement of the hands.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define wavelength. *[1 mark]*

Plane waves generated on the surface of a ripple tank are found to travel $0.74\,\mathrm{m}$ in $1.6\,\mathrm{s}$. The distance between a crest and an adjacent trough is $0.06\,\mathrm{m}$. Calculate: (ii) the average speed of the wave; (iii) the wavelength of the wave; (iv) the frequency of the wave. *[2 + 2 + 2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Wavelength is the **distance between two successive crests (or troughs)**, that is, one complete wave.

(ii) $v = \dfrac{0.74}{1.6} = 0.4625 \approx 0.46\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

(iii) A crest and the adjacent trough are **half** a wavelength apart: $\lambda = 2\times 0.06 = 0.12\,\mathrm{m}$.

(iv) $f = \dfrac{v}{\lambda} = \dfrac{0.4625}{0.12} \approx 3.9\,\mathrm{Hz}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define the principal focus of a converging lens. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Draw a ray diagram to show how a converging lens is used as a magnifying glass. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The principal focus is the **point on the principal axis to which rays travelling parallel to the axis converge after refraction** through the lens.

(ii) Place the object **between the lens and its principal focus**. Draw one ray from the top of the object parallel to the axis, refracted through the focus on the far side; draw a second ray through the optical centre, undeviated. The refracted rays diverge, so trace them back: they meet behind the object, giving a **virtual, upright, magnified image**. *(Figure to be produced.)*
